page.layout: One page of running text. Marginal notes in the left margin, beside paragraphs 4, 5 and 6. Printed page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: socium, parem, coaequalem mihi. Est autem de Christo intelligendum, quia Christus de se hoc citat testimonium. Iohan.10. Ego & Pater unum sumus. Iohan.5. Æqualem se faciens Deo. Item, Ego in Patre, Pater in me. Iohan.10. Facis te Deum, cum sis homo.
Deinde, quomodo igitur Patres refutarunt Arium, si scripturis non potuit convinci? Quomodo verum illud, scripturam valere ad ἔλεγχον? Augustinus contra Maximin. demonstrat id ex sacra scriptura.

p.i: 4. Duas esse naturas in Christo, humanam & divinam, articulus est ad salutem cognitu necessarius. At non est in Scripturis.

main_text.p: Resp. Falsissimum hoc est. Iohan.10. Potestatem habeo ponendi Animam, & potestatem habeo iterum sumendi eam. Ergo Deus & homo. 2. Corinth.13. Mortuus ex infirmitate, vivit ex virtute Dei. 1 Petr.3. Mortificatus quidem carne, vivificatus autem spiritu, &c.

p.i: 5. De duabus in Christo voluntatibus nihil esse expressum in Scripturis.

main_text.p: Resp. Imo 1. sunt in Christo duæ naturæ distinctæ, humana & divina: Ergo duæ voluntates. Utraque enim suam habet voluntatem. 2. Patres damnarunt Monotheletas in Concilio Constantinopolitano 6 ex scripturis, Ergo &c. 3. Luc.22. Pater, transfer at calixi-fte: veruntamen non mea, sed tua voluntas fiat.

p.i: 6. De anima & mente Christi nihil esse in sacra Scriptura.

page.notes: Printed line "Ego & Pater" and similar: the ampersand is as printed. Before "Æqualem" and before "At non est" the printer set a small dingbat or Greek-like mark (a reference sign); it could not be read with certainty and is omitted. "trans:at" in the Luke quotation is doubtful (possibly "transfer a me"). "ἔλεγχον" is a Greek word as printed, read with some uncertainty. The left margin has faint marks, not text, and was left out. Printing as found: "Resp." sits alone at the foot, the paragraph continues on the next page.
